citeAs: Conneau, A., Ma, M., Khanuja, S., Zhang, Y., Axelrod, V., Dalmia, S., Riesa, J., Rivera, C., Bapna, A. (2022). FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech. arXiv:2205.12446.
creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna (Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University)
description: FLEURS (Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech) is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It contains natural human speech and high quality transcripts, and can be used for a variety of speech tasks including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification, Translation, and Retrieval.

name: FLEURS
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (three recordings per sentence by three different native speakers)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were native speakers of each respective language. A sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% was imposed when possible. Train/dev and test sets have disjoint speakers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each sentence, three recordings were collected from three different native speakers. After recording, each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset. A sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% was imposed when possible. Train/dev and test sets have disjoint speakers, with a target ratio of 7:1:2.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset shows performance disparities across geographical groups: results are much better on the Western European group (10.7 average CER) than on Sub-Saharan African (15.6 average CER) or South Asian (17.4 average CER) groups, partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data available for WE languages. The authors note that reducing gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction. Additionally, about 21.5% of sentences are missing due to failed validation, which may not be uniformly distributed across languages.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built on top of FLoRes-101, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia translated into 101 languages by human translators. Only the dev and devtest sets (2009 sentences total) were used, split into new train (1509), dev (150), and test (350) splits. For each sentence in 102 languages, three recordings were collected from three different native speakers, with a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% imposed when possible. After recording, each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponds to the input sentence; invalid recordings were discarded. All segments are within 30 seconds, and the speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. The authors plan to fill these gaps in future versions of the dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source text data comes from FLoRes-101, which contains sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators. Speech recordings were collected from native speakers reading these sentences aloud.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. The dataset covers only 102 languages, and performance varies significantly across language groups. The dataset is based on Wikipedia text (via FLoRes-101), which may not represent all domains or spoken language styles. All recordings are kept as-is from quiet or noisy environments without data augmentation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For textual data, NFC and FST normalization was applied to each sentence, followed by lower-casing, normalization and removal of punctuations. Words were split into characters, with a token for word boundaries. Three versions of each sentence are provided: the original raw transcript (SRC_RAW), the preprocessed version (SRC_NORM), and its character-based version (SRC_CHAR). A universal vocabulary of characters was adopted as the modeling and evaluation unit. For languages like Chinese, Japanese, and Korean that have irregular spacing, special tokenization handling was applied.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, with the aim of building speech technologies for everyone. The dataset spans over 100 languages, including many low-resource ones, to help reduce the gap in speech technology access across different language communities.
rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS is intended for evaluating speech technology across multiple tasks: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval. It is particularly suited for evaluating few-shot and data-efficient multilingual pre-trained representations of speech, and for catalyzing research in low-resource speech understanding.

null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No specific annotation platform (e.g., MTurk, custom tool) is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis are reported beyond the validation/discard process.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; missing recordings are simply discarded and noted as absent.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The paper explicitly states no data augmentations (e.g., SpecAugment, speed perturbation, simulated reverberation) were applied to the dataset recordings.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine annotation tools are described as part of the dataset annotation pipeline; validation was done by human workers.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is discussed in the paper; the dataset contains speech recordings of Wikipedia text.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No formal maintenance plan is described beyond a mention of filling missing data gaps in future versions.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
